Subject: HearthCare - post-call network & residency checklist

Hi Samir / Megan —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone stays aligned and we can move the POC forward. High-level goal: evaluate Redwood Private (VPC peering) for inference of PHI-adjacent telemetry and customer-facing summarization, with an eye towards a 90-day POC and potential Dedicated commitment thereafter.

Key pain points you called out:
- No outbound internet egress from inference hosts; all external calls must go through an approved proxy or NAT egress controlled by HearthCare.
- Data residency: all inference request/response logs and model artifacts must remain in US-East (AWS us-east-1) with retention limited to 30 days unless explicitly tagged for longer.
- Air-gap posture for some workloads: certain business units require isolated subnets with no direct internet and only site-to-site VPN reachability.
- Strict allowlist for outbound IPs and TLS inspection via your perimeter proxy.
- Proofs required for procurement: SOC 2 Type II report, evidence of key management integration approach, and an incident response contact.

Agreed next steps (what we need from HearthCare):
1) Network diagram (VPC/subnets, firewalls, proxies) and the diagram you mentioned in today’s call. (Samir: you said you’d share v3.)
2) IP allowlist targets (if you prefer our egress to be a predictable set of IPs we can provide).
3) Clarify whether the air-gapped workload will accept an SFTP/dropbox for model updates or requires physically loaded media.
4) Exec sponsor & timeline target for the POC decision (you mentioned a July 2028 executive review).

Internal asks (cc’d team):
- Priyom: please prepare a short ops checklist that maps HearthCare constraints to Redwood Private deployment options (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or on-prem appliance). Include implications on latency and estimated token costs.
- Ben: I’ll need a draft commercial note that outlines POC pricing vs Dedicated baseline and a list of the procurement artifacts we can supply.
- Laura: can you prepare an SOW template for a 90-day POC with a removable dedicated pool option?

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with our infra engineer and your network lead once we have the diagram.

Thanks again — appreciate the clarity on the constraints.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — I pulled the diagram and have a short ops mapping below. Will follow with a one-page PDF for the call.

Immediate technical notes (high level):
- Customer-initiated VPN: supported if we deploy the Redwood Private appliance into a customer-controlled subnet and configure IKEv2 with our public keys; this is our typical pattern for isolated customers. Expect a small config window (1–2 business days) and potential certificate exchange.
- Fixed egress IPs: we can front the egress with a NAT gateway in our managed cloud tenancy and publish up to 8 static IPs per POC environment. If HearthCare needs <=10, we should be able to satisfy it by reserving an extra IP or using a short-lived NAT translation pool. Note: scaling beyond this pattern requires a different topology and will affect cost.
- TLS inspection & caching: if TLS is terminated at their proxy, our prefix/KV caching must be colocated inside the customer perimeter to maintain privacy guarantees. That implies either (a) containerized cache deployed in their VPC with access to the runtime, or (b) a policy where caching is disabled for private workloads. Option (a) has added ops complexity but preserves cost benefits.
- Log retention: we can set default retention to 30 days; KV caches can be configured to flush to zero after 24 hours for PII-sensitive flows. Need legal/compliance to confirm acceptable durations.

Next steps I’ll own:
- Create an ops checklist and two recommended topologies (customer-initiated VPN + NAT egress vs appliance in their subnet) — will deliver a PDF by Monday EOD.
- Join the technical deep-dive and bring one infra engineer to walk the diagram.

Ben / Laura: confirm if you want me to include estimated latency numbers for both topologies.
